narrative:
On August 10, 2026, the Karnataka High Court scheduled 2,648 cases across 39 judges, hearing 996 of them to achieve an overall hearing rate of 37.6%. This represents a slight reduction from the 39.6% rate recorded on August 7 (936 heard of 2,363 scheduled) and remains below the recent peak of 45.6% recorded on August 6 (1,167 heard of 2,560 scheduled).

Judicial throughput varied substantially across court halls. Justice V Srishananda in Hall 21 demonstrated strong efficiency, hearing 68 of 93 scheduled cases (73.1%), while Justice Chillakur Sumalatha in Hall 25 achieved a 74.1% clearance rate (40 of 54 heard). Justice M. Nagaprasanna managed substantial volume in Hall 14, hearing 96 of 200 cases (48.0%) on his primary list. Conversely, Hall 6 under Justice B M Shyam Prasad saw 0 of 151 scheduled cases heard, and Justice Suraj Govindaraj converted lower percentages across large dockets in Halls 10 and 11, hearing 20.7% (29 of 140) and 26.2% (38 of 145) respectively.

Analysis by hearing stage shows that Orders formed the largest share of scheduled matters at 736 cases, achieving a 44.7% conversion rate (329 heard), closely mirroring August 7 levels (43.7%). Admission matters converted at 42.1% (189 of 449 heard), whereas Final Hearing conversion dropped to 17.8% (99 of 556 heard) compared to 23.5% on August 7. By case type, Writ Petitions (WP) comprised the heaviest load with 1,256 cases, but logged a lower hearing rate of 31.0% (389 heard) compared to 38.3% on August 7. Criminal Petitions (CRL.P) and Miscellaneous First Appeals (MFA) posted conversion rates of 42.1% (165 of 392) and 41.8% (162 of 388) respectively, while Regular Second Appeals (RSA) achieved a higher clearance efficiency of 62.1% (72 of 116 heard).
